requested.title: Active agent runs retain project and repository authority after member removal

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: The VM route authenticates the caller as the sandbox assigned to a run, deriving `runId` from the signed sandbox identity, but this proves only possession of an active run identity rather than current project membership. `handleControlPlaneRequest` loads the run with the service-role client and validates only sandbox-name consistency; it never calls `getProjectAccess(run.created_by, run.project_id)` or an equivalent revocation check. For a non-PR cloud run, `POST /repo-auth` subsequently calls `resolveRepoCloneTarget(run.project_id, "repo-write")`, whose project-only resolver reads the link and mints a scoped GitHub installation token without checking the run creator's current access. Thus, a member can start a cloud agent run while authorized, be removed through `removeMember` (which only deletes the `project_members` row), and the still-running sandbox can renew repository write credentials and push to that repository. No member-removal path cancels matching active runs, stops their sandboxes, or revokes existing run keys; the normal reapers act only on terminal/idle or dead-run conditions. Some issue, page, objective, and routine helpers independently re-check an `actorId` against current access, so stale project-tool mutation is not universal, but that does not mitigate the repository-token path. Current history shows sandbox identity binding and token scoping improvements, not a membership revalidation or removal-triggered run revocation, so the reported vulnerability remains present and exploitable.
